caption:
Google Ads AI review summaries checklist: 4 things small business and Black-owned business owners should fix now.

Google is now showing AI-written review summaries inside Search ads. Its help page says Google AI gathers reviews from across the web and turns them into short, positive commentary shown with your ad. Advertisers can't edit the text, and the page lists no way to turn it off. PPC Land and The Keyword reported it on October 24 to 26, 2026. It runs on English Search campaigns in the US, UK, Australia and India.

So the way customers describe you is turning into ad copy. Here's what to tighten up first:
1. One clear line on your website that says what you do and who it's for.
2. The same business name, logo and photos on Google, Yelp, Facebook and Instagram.
3. A simple ask after every job that tells happy customers where to leave a review.
4. Replies to your reviews that sound like you, every time.

At Blackwell Graphics we build brand identities, logos and websites for Black-owned businesses, so your promise is clear before the first review is written. DM us "REVIEWS" to talk it through, or visit blackwellgraphics.com (link in bio).

caption_drafts.explainer:
Google Ads now adds AI review summaries to Search ads, and small business owners can't edit them.

Google's help page for review summaries says its AI gathers online reviews from across the web and turns them into short commentary shown with your ad. Google says the summaries are only positive, and it shows them only when it predicts they will improve ad performance. They run on English Search campaigns in the US, UK, Australia and India.

The part that matters for a Black-owned business: Google says advertisers cannot edit or customize the generated text, because it represents customer feedback. What customers say about you across the web now feeds the ad you pay for.

caption_drafts.provocation:
If Google's AI wrote one line about your small business in your next ad, what would it say?

That's happening now. Google is showing AI-written review summaries inside Search ads in the US, UK, Australia and India. Google AI pulls reviews from across the web and writes short, positive commentary next to your ad. You can't edit it, and Google's help page lists no off switch.

Picture two Black-owned salons running the same ad. One has reviews that keep saying "clean, on time, worth it." The other has scattered reviews on three sites under two different names. Google's AI has very different material to work with.
